structured.answer: If I have to choose, I'd take "כספי (שקלי)": it shows 0% מניות and 0% מט"ח, it's in shekels, and it's the only safe-looking one with a number, 4.25%. "אג"ח סחיר" also has no shares, but it only says "פחות מ־3 שנים". I'm not signing anything until you or the bank tell me what "כספי" means and whether 0.57% is a lot to pay.

stuck.where: Screen 1, the two rows of track buttons
stuck.why: Most of the names mean nothing to me (S&P 500, עוקב מדדים, גמיש, קיימות). I only looked for something with אג"ח or something that sounds like plain money.
Too many numbers and coloured circles on a black background. I followed only the rows where shares showed 0%.

stuck.where: Screen 2, 'פחות מ־3 שנים' in the return column
stuck.why: I didn't know whether that means the track is new or something bad. Because of it, the bond track had no number and I couldn't compare it.

stuck.where: Choosing between אג"ח סחיר and כספי (שקלי)
stuck.why: I trust bonds, but 'סחיר' sounds like trading. I don't know what 'כספי' means, but it had 0/0 and a number I could understand.
